rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial mīm takes fatḥa to resolve three consecutive vowelless letters; Zajjāj says no other pronunciation is possible.
rows.anchor: لا يسوغ في اللفظ أن ينطق بثلاثة أحرف سواكن فلا بد من فتحة الميم

rows.speaker: الرؤاسي
rows.claim: A report ascribed to al-Ruʾāsī transfers the hamza vowel and reads alif-lām-mīm followed by Allāh; Zajjāj says this is not soundly transmitted from ʿĀṣim.
rows.anchor: عن الرؤاسي، فائا من رواه عن عاصم فليس بصحيح الرواية

rows.speaker: بعض النحويين
rows.claim: Some grammarians argue the vowel for meeting two sukūns should be kasra, but Zajjāj rejects this because kasra after yāʾ is heavy, as in impossible kayfa Zayd and ayna Zayd.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض النحويين لو كانت محركة للالتقاء الساكنين لكانث مكسورة

rows.speaker: الأخفش وأبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Al-Akhfash and Abū ʿUbayda take dhālika al-kitāb to mean this book, supported by a poetic use of dhālika for hādhā.
rows.anchor: زعم الأخفش وأبو عبيدة أن معناه هذا الكتاب

rows.speaker: غيرهما من النحويين
rows.claim: Other grammarians identify it as the Qurʾān promised through Moses and Jesus, citing earlier scripture-holders recognizing it and concealing the truth.
rows.anchor: وقال غيرهما من النحويين: إن معناه القرآن ذلك الكتاب الذي وعدوا به على لسان موسى وعيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika can point back to something already mentioned just as hādhā can; Zajjāj illustrates the alternation with arithmetic and Qurʾānic examples.
rows.anchor: انفقت ثلاثة وثلاثة فذلك ستة وإن شئت قلت هذا ستة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan can be a second predicate, giving the sense that this is both the promised Book and guidance, like something combining two qualities.
rows.anchor: إحداها أن يكون خبرا بعد خبر كأنه قال: هذا ذلك الكتاب هدى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan may be nominative with an omitted huwa after the sentence about the Book is complete.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكلون رفعه على إضمار هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hudan may also be parsed as a confirmation of the Book's being true, followed by the separate statement that it contains guidance.
rows.anchor: كأنك قلت ذلك الكتاب حقا، لأن لا شك فيه بمعنى حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To believe in something means to affirm it.
rows.anchor: معناه يصدقون، وكل مؤمن بشيء فهو مصدق به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Used without naming what is believed, muʾmin is properly applicable only to God, according to Zajjāj.
rows.anchor: فإذا ذكرت مؤمنا ولم تقل هو مؤمن بكذا وكذا فهو الذي لا يصلح إلا في الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ladhīna may be genitive as an adjective dependent on al-muttaqīn.
rows.anchor: وموضع (الذين) جر تبعا للمتقين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ladhīna may instead be nominative as praise, framed as an answer to who the God-fearing are.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون موضعهم رفعا على المدح كأنه لما قيل هدى للمتقين قيل من هم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third parse puts al-ladhīna in the accusative as an imperative of praise: remember those who believe.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون موضع الذين نصبا على المدح أيضا كأنه قيل اذكر الذين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular and plural relative forms are indeclinable because they remain incomplete until their relative clauses and resemble particles; the plural form is treated like a singular collective.
rows.anchor: والذي والذين مبهمان لا تتمان إلا بصلاتهما فلذلك منعت الإعراب

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه والأخفش
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl, Sībawayh, al-Akhfash, and trusted authorities derive alladhī from ladh, on the pattern of ʿamr.
rows.anchor: وأصل - الذي لذ على وزن عم فاعلم، كذلك قال الخليل وسيبويه والأخفش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dual inflects although the singular relative is indeclinable because dualization removes its resemblance to a meaning-bearing particle, and particles do not form duals.
rows.anchor: لأن حروف المعاني لا تثنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural remains indeclinable because a non-dual plural behaves like the singular; hāʾulāʾ and alladhīna each function as a single collective noun.
rows.anchor: لأن الجمع الذي ليس على حد التثنية كالواحد، ألا ترى أنك قلت في جميع هذا هؤلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant ḥidhār al-mawt is also transmitted, but the readers in Zajjāj's region read ḥadhar al-mawt.
rows.anchor: حذار الموت، والذي عليه قراؤنا (حذر الموت)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥadhara is an accusative of cause, meaning they do this from fear of death; it is a verbal noun in sense, not an accusative caused by dropping the preposition lām.
rows.anchor: وليس نصبه لسقوط اللام، وإنما نصبه أنه في تأويل المصدر كأنه قال يحذرون حذرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anonymous poetic example uses idhkhāra to mean for the sake of saving or preserving, supporting the causal accusative analysis.
rows.anchor: وأغفر عوراء الكريم ادخاره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God argues with the Arabs from what they already acknowledge: He created them and those before them, so they should worship Him rather than idols.
rows.anchor: إن الله احتج على العرب بأنه خالقهم وخالق من قبلهم لأنهم كانوا مقرين بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tattaqūn means guarding yourselves from forbidden things and refraining from what God prohibited.
rows.anchor: معناه تتقون الحرمات بينكم وتكفون عما تأتون مما حرمه الله

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists interpret laʿalla causally here as meaning so that you may become God-fearing.
rows.anchor: عن بعض أهل اللغة: أحدهما: معناها كي تتقوا، والذي يذهب إليه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh takes laʿalla in such contexts as expressing hope; Zajjāj follows this analysis, illustrated by Moses and Aaron hoping Pharaoh might remember while God knows the outcome.
rows.anchor: والذي يذهب إليه سيبويه في مثل هذا أنه ترج لهم كما قال في قصة فرعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyu is an indeclinable singular vocative, and al-nās is its required adjective; yāʾ cannot directly precede a definite noun, so ayyu provides access to the article.
rows.anchor: وأما إعراب (يا أيها) فأي اسم مبهم مبني على الضم لأنه منادى مفرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The attention particle hāʾ is required with ayyu and substitutes for its usual annexation, since ayyu is normally annexed in interrogative or declarative use.
rows.anchor: وها لازمه لأي، للتنبيه، وهي عوض من الإضافة في أي

rows.speaker: سيبويه عن الخليل
rows.claim: Sībawayh reports al-Khalīl's analysis: a singular vocative is built on the nominative form, so its adjective has regular nominative case.
rows.anchor: زعم سيبويه عن الخليل أن المنادى المفرد مبني وصفته مرفوعة رفعا صحيحا

rows.speaker: المازني
rows.claim: Al-Māzinī permits an accusative adjective by analogy with the vocative's underlying accusative position; Zajjāj notes other grammarians do not accept this for yā ayyuhā al-rajul.
rows.anchor: والمازني يجيز في يا أيها الرجل النصب في الرجل، ولم يقل بهذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the vocative's true target is al-rajul and ayyu is only a link to it, Arab usage in yā ayyuhā consistently raises the adjective.
rows.anchor: والنحويون لا يقولون إلا يا أيها الرجل، يا أيها الناس، والعرب لغتها في هذا الرفع

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الأخفش
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Akhfash says it is more analogical for al-rajul to serve as a complement to ayyu, but no Basran grammarian follows him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الحسن الأخفش إن الرجل أن يكون صلة لأي أقيس، وليس أحد من البصريين يتابعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth as firāsh is a spread-out resting place, neither rugged nor so hard and thick that settling on it is impossible.
rows.anchor: معناه وطاء، لم يجعلها حزنة غليظة لا يمكن الاستقرار عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bināʾ names anything raised above the earth; here it means God made the sky a roof.
rows.anchor: ومعناه إنه جعلها سقفا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both assimilation and clear pronunciation are possible in jaʿala lakum; most readers use clear pronunciation because the words are separate.
rows.anchor: ويجوز في قوله: (جعل لكم الأرض) وجهان: الإدغام والإظهار، تقول: جعل لكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Andād means counterparts or equals; God argues that people who know idols do not create must not make them God's peers.
rows.anchor: لا تجعلوا لله أمثالا وأنتم تعلمون أنهم لا يخلقون والله الخالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arab lexemes nidd and nadīd mean a peer; Jarīr's verse supplies evidence for nidd.
rows.anchor: قال جرير: أتيما تجعلون إلي ندا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This verse and the one before it establish God's oneness; the following challenge to produce a sūra establishes the Prophet's truth, and rayb means doubt.
rows.anchor: فهذه الآية والتي قبلها احتجاج عليهم في تثبيت توحيد الله عز وجل. ثم احتج عليهم فيما يلي هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is nominative despite its interrogative form, with the sense who is more unjust; aẓlam is the predicate of the initial clause.
rows.anchor: موضع (من) رفع ولفظها لفظ استفهام، المعنى: وأي أحد أظلم ممن منع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause an yudhkara is accusative as an appositive to masājid Allāh, meaning preventing God's name from being mentioned in the mosques.
rows.anchor: وموضع أن نصب على البدل من مساجد الله، المعنى: ومن أظلم ممن منع أن يذكر في مساجد الله اسمه

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: One exegetical identification is the Romans, who entered and ruined Jerusalem's sanctuary.
rows.anchor: جاء في التفسير أن هذا يعني به الروم، لأنهم كانوا دخلوا بيت المقدس وخربوه

rows.speaker: التفسير
rows.claim: Another identification is the Meccan polytheists, who sought to stop Muslims from remembering God in the Sacred Mosque.
rows.anchor: وقيل يعني به مشركو مكة لأنهم سعوا في منع المسلمين من ذكر الله في المسجد الحرام

rows.speaker: بعض أهل اللغة
rows.claim: Some linguists apply the verse to all unbelievers opposing Islam and preventing prayer throughout the mosques; any place of worship is a mosque, as the Prophet's report that earth was made a mosque and purification indicates.
rows.anchor: زعم أنه يعني به جميع الكفار الذين تظاهروا على الإسلام، ومنعوا جملة المساجد

words: أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ مَا كَانَ لَهُمْ أَن يَدْخُلُوهَآ إِلَّا خَآئِفِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God says the Muslim community will prevail over its opponents until no opponent can enter its mosques except in fear.
rows.anchor: أعلم الله في هذه الآية أن أمر المسلمين يظهر على جميع من خالفهم حتى لا يمكن دخول مخالف إلى مساجدهم إلا خائفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khizyun can be nominative as a new subject or as the subject of an implied verb associated with lahum; the sense is that humiliation is due them.
rows.anchor: يرتفع (خزي) من وجهتين: إحداهما الابتداء، والأخرى الفعل الذي ينوب عنه (لهم).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly humiliation is being killed if they are at war and charged jizya if they are protected non-Muslims.
rows.anchor: والخزي الذي لهم في الدنيا، أن يقتلوا إن كانوا حربا، ويجزوا إن كانوا ذمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment is described as great because they are the most unjust, as the verse's opening states.
rows.anchor: وجعل لهم عظيم العذاب لأنهم أظلم من ظلم لقوله: (ومن أظلم ممن منع).

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-mashriq and al-maghrib admit the two nominative parses just described for khizyun; lillāh means God created both.
rows.anchor: يرتفعان كما وصفنا من جهتين، ومعنى (لله) أي هو خالقهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means looking toward the sky; it is also explained as the movement of the eyes, since the Prophet awaited revelation after being told to stop praying toward Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: المعنى: في النظر إلى السماء، وقيل: تقلب عينك، والمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqallub is the regular verbal noun; taqlāban is possible in speech but not in Qurʾānic text because it would alter the written muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: وتقلب مصدر تقلب تقلبا، ويجوز في الكلام تقلابا، ولا يجوز في القرآن لأنه تغيير للمصحف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: While in Medina, the Prophet was ordered to change prayer direction from Jerusalem to the Sacred House in Mecca.
rows.anchor: قد كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالمدينة حين أمر بأن ينتقل عن الصلاة إلى بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: One interpretation takes tardāhā as you love it, without implying the Prophet was displeased with the former qibla, since prophets accept what God commands.
rows.anchor: قال قوم معناه تحبها، لا أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لم يكن راضيا بتلك القبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet loved the new qibla, according to reports, because it had been the qibla of earlier prophets.
rows.anchor: وإنما أحبها النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لأنها كانت - فيما يروى - قبلة الأنبياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reported reason for loving it is that this qibla would more readily draw his people to faith.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأنها كانت عنده ادعى لقومه إلى الإيمان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shatra means toward or in the direction of; the command was to face Mecca and the Sacred House, including for people wherever they were, and shatra is an accusative of place or direction.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الشطر: النحو. وشطر منصوب على الظرف.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anonymous verse's shatrah means toward it, confirming the directional sense of shatr.
rows.anchor: إن العسير بها داء يخامرها. . . فشطرها نظر العينين محسور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shāṭir describes someone who has turned from the straight path toward another direction.
rows.anchor: فلذلك قيل شاطر لعدوله عن الاستواء، يقال قد شطر الرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase qawm mushāṭirūnā means their houses adjoin ours; the usage compares people whose directions lie toward one another.
rows.anchor: هؤلاء قوم مشاطرونا أي دورهم تتصل بدورنا

words: إلا لنعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن ينقلب على عقبيه
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows future obedience before it happens, but the verse means knowing it as witnessed so people earn the names obedient or disobedient and are rewarded for deeds; what is witnessed was already known as unseen.
rows.anchor: فالجواب في ذلك أن الله يعلم من يتبع الرسول ممن لا يتبعه من قبل وقوعه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh says the disputed wāw is open to resolve two adjacent sukūns; some of his colleagues say it is built on fatḥ, which is also consistent with his account of the imperfect lām, and both analyses are possible.
rows.anchor: فقال سيبويه: إنها مفتوحة لالتقاء الساكنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular shayʾ compresses a repeated phrase: a thing of fear, a thing of hunger, and a thing of loss in wealth, lives, and fruits.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل بأشياء، فإنما جاء على الاختصار، والمعنى يدل على أنه وشيء من الخوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trials make the companions' steadfastness persuasive to later people and contemporaries: endurance shows that truth and proof were clear; God grants the afflicted what benefits them in this life and the next.
rows.anchor: لأنهم يعلمون أنه لا يصبر على هذه الأشياء إلا من قد وضح له الحق وبان له البرهان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The saying means that the people and their property belong to God, are His servants, and He may do with them as He wills; this contains benefit and good for them.
rows.anchor: أي نحن وأموالنا لله ونحن عبيده يصنع بنا ما شاء، وفي ذلك صلاح لنا وخير.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Returning to God means affirming resurrection and reward for belief and for patience under trial.
rows.anchor: أي نحن مصدقون بأنا نبعث ونعطي الثواب على تصديقنا، والصبر على ما ابتلانا به.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God makes matters easier by exempting the sick and travelers from fasting.
rows.anchor: أي أن ييسر عليكم بوضعه عنكم الصوم في السفر والمرض.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both a doubled and a light lām form are read: litukammilū from kammala and litakmalū from kamula.
rows.anchor: بالتشديد، ولتكملوا بالتخفيف. من كمل يكمل، وأكمل يكمل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction continues according to the sense: God did this to ease matters and to let you complete the number; the poem coordinates mushajjaj with an implied baqiyat after bādat illā rawākid.
rows.anchor: معطوف محمول على المعنى. (المعنى) فعل الله ذلك ليسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If asked where God is, He is near and no place is devoid of Him; Zajjāj supports this with the verses about God's presence in confidential conversation and being with people wherever they are.
rows.anchor: فالله عز وجل قريب لا يخلو منه مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One may pronounce daʿānī with yāʾ or omit the yāʾ; pausing follows the written muṣḥaf.
rows.anchor: إن شئت قلت إذا دعاني بياء وإن شئت بغير ياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One kind of calling on God is affirming His oneness and praising Him; the command to call in 40:60 includes this worship.
rows.anchor: فضرب منها توحيده والثناء عليه كقولك يا الله لا إله إلا أنت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second kind of duʿāʾ asks God for pardon, mercy, and related benefits.
rows.anchor: وضرب ثان هو مسألة الله العفو والرحمة، وما يقرب منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third kind asks for worldly provisions such as wealth and children.
rows.anchor: وضرب ثالث هو مسألته من الدنيا كقولك: اللهم ارزقني مالا وولدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three are called duʿāʾ because a person begins them by saying O Allah, O Lord, or O Ever-Living.
rows.anchor: وإنما سمي هذا أجمع دعاء لأن الإنسان يصدر في هذه الأشياء بقوله يا الله، ويا رب، ويا حي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here their unbelief in those places is worse than killing.
rows.anchor: أي فكفرهم في هذه الأمكنة أشد من القتل.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muslims were forbidden to initiate killing or fighting at the Sacred Mosque until the polytheists began hostilities.
rows.anchor: كانوا قد نهوا عن ابتدائهم بقتل أو قتال حتى يبتدي المشركون بذلك.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A variant reads lā taqtulūhum ḥattā yaqtulūkum, do not kill them until they kill you, expressing the same rule against initiating killing.
rows.anchor: وتقرأ: (ولا تقتلوهم عند المسجد الحرام حتى يقتلوكم فيه)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic may say qatalta al-qawma even when only some of the group were killed, if context makes that intended meaning clear.
rows.anchor: وجائز ولا تقتلوهم وإن وقع القتل ببعض دون بعض، لأن اللغة يجوز فيها قتلت القوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is to fight every unbeliever, since fitna in this passage means unbelief; if they desist, aggression is only against wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: هذا أمر من الله عز وجل أن يقاتل كل كافر لأن المعنى - ههنا في الفتنة والكفر.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿajjala means to depart after two days.
rows.anchor: أي من نفر في يومين.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the pilgrim who avoids hunting game may depart early without sin.
rows.anchor: قيل لمن اتقى قتل الصيد، وقالوا: لمن اتقى التفريط في كل حدود الحج.

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that the pilgrim avoids neglecting all the obligations of pilgrimage; early departure is then permitted.
rows.anchor: وقالوا: لمن اتقى التفريط في كل حدود الحج. فموسع عليه في التعجل في نفره.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Man is nominative under either of two parses: as the initial subject or through the governing factor in min.
rows.anchor: موضع (من) رفع على ضربين: على الابتداء، وبالعامل في (من)

rows.speaker: رجل من ثقيف
rows.claim: A report says a man from Thaqīf impressed the Prophet with his speech while inwardly concealing the opposite of his attractive outward presentation.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن رجلا من ثقيف كان يعجب النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كلامه

words: وَيُشْهِدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ مَا فِى قَلْبِهِۦ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the form yashhadu Allāh is read, it is valid and means God knows what the hypocrite keeps secret, thereby informing the Prophet of his true condition.
rows.anchor: وإن قلت ويشهد الله على ما في قلبه فهو جائز إن كان قد قرئ به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aladd al-khiṣām means fierce in disputation; its derivation is from the two sides of the neck, since he prevails whichever direction an argument takes.
rows.anchor: ومعنى خصم ألد في اللغة - الشديد الخصومة والجدل، واشتقاقه من لديدي العنق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The forms are aladd for a man, ladāʾ for a woman, and ladd for a group; lidadtu fulānan means I argued with and defeated him.
rows.anchor: يقال رجل ألد، وامرأة لداء وقوم لد - وقد لددت فلانا ألده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khiṣām can pluralize khiṣm as an adjective, alongside khuṣūm; when khiṣm is a noun, fiʿāl is the larger plural, as in farakh, afrākh, firākh, and furūkh.
rows.anchor: وخصام جمع خصم، لأن فعلا يجمع إذا كان صفة على فعال، نحو صعب وصعاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Li-yufsida is accusative after an understood an, meaning in order to corrupt; wa-yuhlika may be coordinated with it or begin a new clause with an omitted huwa.
rows.anchor: نصب (ليفسد) على إضمار أن، المعنى لأن يفسد فيها، وعطف ويهلك

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: One reported interpretation takes al-ḥarth and al-nasl as women and children; this is plausible because a woman is called ḥarth, by comparison with what is cultivated and bears produce.
rows.anchor: وقالوا في (الحرث والنسل): إن الحرث النساء والنسل الأولاد.

rows.speaker: قالوا
rows.claim: Another interpretation keeps al-ḥarth as crops: corruption and disorder in the land ruin agriculture.
rows.anchor: وقالوا في الحرث هو ما تعرفه من الزرع. لأنه إذا أفسد في الأرض أبطل

rows.speaker: أهل اللغة
rows.claim: The language authorities explain yashrī nafsahu as selling oneself, meaning giving oneself in jihad for God's sake.
rows.anchor: قال أهل اللغة - (يشري نفسه) يبيع نفسه، ومعنى بيعه نفسه بذلها في الجهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The anonymous poem uses sharaytu to mean I sold, witnessing the lexical sense of yashrī.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر في شريت بمعنى بعت: وشريت بردا ليتني

rows.speaker: أهل التفسير
rows.claim: Exegetes identify the person as Ṣuhayb ibn Sinān: after the polytheists killed some companions and demanded that he abandon Islam, he offered his wealth in return for being allowed to leave; in Medina Abū Bakr called it a profitable sale and Ṣuhayb recited the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال أهل التفسير هذا رجل كان يقال له صهيب بن سنان.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtighāʾa is an accusative of purpose: he gives himself in order to seek God's approval.
rows.anchor: ونصب (ابتغاء مرضات الله) على معنى المفغول له.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine noun ṭāliq is used without tāʾ in ṭāliq, while ṭallaqat al-marʾatu and ṭuliqat are also reported forms.
rows.anchor: يقال طلقت المرأة طلاقا فهي طالق، وقد حكوا طلقت

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some claim the feminine tāʾ is omitted from ṭāliq because the word only applies to women; Zajjāj rejects this since many shared masculine-feminine descriptors lack tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقد زعم قوم أن تاء التأنيث حذفت من

rows.speaker: سيبويه وأصحابه
rows.claim: Sībawayh and his colleagues analyze ṭāliq as a masculine-form adjective applied to a feminine noun, underlyingly something divorced or dhāt ṭalāq, like descriptors meaning a bearer of sons, daughters, or a child.
rows.anchor: وزعم سيبويه وأصحابه أن هذا وقع على لفظ التذكير صفة للمؤنث لأن المعنى شيء طالق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When ṭāliq is derived directly from the verb, the feminine form is ṭāliqa; al-Aʿshā's verse addresses a woman as ṭāliqa.
rows.anchor: فإذا أجريته على الفعل قلت طالقة. قال الأعشى:

rows.speaker: أهل الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufans understand qurūʾ as menstrual periods.
rows.anchor: فأما أهل الكوفة فيقولون: الأقراء الحيض

rows.speaker: أهل الحجاز ومالك
rows.claim: The Hijazis and Mālik understand qurūʾ as periods of purity.
rows.anchor: وأما أهل الحجاز ومالك فيقولون الأقراء الطهر

rows.speaker: أم سلمة
rows.claim: The Kufans cite Umm Salama's report about Fāṭima bint Abī Ḥubays: she was told to wait through her menstrual days and wash outside them.
rows.anchor: ما يروى عن أم سلمة إنها استفتت لفاطمة بنت أبي حبيش وكانت مستحاضة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A second report says when Fāṭima's qurʾ arrives she should not pray; after it passes she should purify herself and pray until the next qurʾ.
rows.anchor: وفي خبر آخر أن فاطمة سألته فقال إذا أتى قرؤك فلا تصلي

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī says qurʾ means menstruation and aqraʾat al-marʾatu means she menstruated, strengthening the Kufan interpretation.
rows.anchor: الذي يقويه من مذهب أهل اللغة أن الأصمعي كان يقول: القرء الحيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qurʾ conveys gathering: it can mean blood gathering in the body during purity or gathering in the womb during menstruation, so both juristic interpretations are sound and the distinction reconciles them; miqraʾa and miqraʾ also name containers where water or provisions gather.
rows.anchor: فإنما القرء اجتماع الدم في البدن، وذلك إنما يكون في الطهر، وقد يكون اجتماعه في الرحم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says women must not conceal a pregnancy, since doing so could assign the child to someone other than its father.
rows.anchor: قيل فيه لا يحل لهن أن يكتمن أمر الولد لأنهن إن فعلن ذلك

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Another view identifies what is concealed as menstruation; Zajjāj prefers the child interpretation because God's creation in wombs more directly suggests the child, as other verses describe forming people there.
rows.anchor: وقد قال قوم هو الحيض. وهو بالولد أشبه لأن ما خلق الله في أرحامهن أدل على الولد

words: إِن كُنَّ يُؤْمِنَّ بِٱللَّهِ وَٱلْيَوْمِ ٱلْءَاخِرِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condition means that belief in God's threats and punishment for grave sins should restrain them from concealment, just as one tells an unjust person that faith should keep him from oppression.
rows.anchor: تأويله إن كن يصدقن بالله وبما أرهب به وخوف من عذابه لأهل الكبائر
